1. A review can merge unreviewed commits 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The review protocol waits for checks by pull request number and merges without verifying that the
>head still matches the commit its sub-agents reviewed. If the mission branch advances during the
>review, the review can record the earlier headRefOid while the later commit passes checks and is
>merged.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[R275-279]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-1a13ad1e2168d9dd38e2e3f07712fc77e6d7bbef5b55f45f54dbd1737103bfb6R275-R279) > >```diff >+With `pull_request` and `blockers=0`, the review's own commit has started >+the checks again, so first wait for them — `hands ci-wait ; echo >+"ci-wait-exit=$?"`, one foreground call at a time, again while it exits 3, >+at most seven calls — and merge only on exit 0, as above (`gh pr merge >+ --merge --subject "merge: mission N (PR #)"`, then `git >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Merging without pinning or rechecking the reviewed head permits commits added after review to merge
>unreviewed.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The protocol identifies the reviewed commit as the PR's headRefOid, but both waits use `hands
>ci-wait <number> and the merge command supplies no expected head SHA. ci_wait` queries checks for
>the PR's current head and accepts no SHA argument.
>
> > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[46-70\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L46-L70) > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[203-217\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L203-L217) > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[275-283\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L275-L283) > [src/hands/cli.py\[197-207\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/cli.py/#L197-L207) > [src/hands/forge.py\[168-178\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/forge.py/#L168-L178) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The pull-request review can merge a branch head that changed after the reviewed commit was selected. >## Fix Focus Areas >- templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[203-217] >- templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[275-283] >- meta/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[275-283] >## Recommended Fix >Require the fetched review tip to match the pull request head, recheck that head before accepting checks, and merge with a head-commit match condition. If it changed, stop for another review; update both protocol copies. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

2. Applies from main take the mission-branch path and fail 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>PULL_REQUEST_APPLY case (b) treats main as an in-flight mission branch because it is on
>origin, is not a kit/ branch, and has no MERGED or CLOSED head pull requests. When an apply
>starts on main between missions, the builder commits and attempts to push there instead of opening
>the kit pull request; protected main refuses the push, and the resulting kit not applied pr=none
>reply stops the pipeline through _apply_not_landed.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/kit.py[R227-230]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-c741f63d4fccb12bbfc566ee658f6a10d5d610c9e09e4a336f11292aaa5c1b37R227-R230) > >```diff >+ "(b) On another branch, not a `kit/` one, that is on `origin` (`git ls-remote", >+ "--exit-code --heads origin `) and whose pull requests, if it has", >+ "any, are all open (`gh pr list --head --state all --json state`", >+ "names none `MERGED` or `CLOSED`), a mission is in flight on it: unzip -o into", >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Normal apply from main matches case (b), causing a protected-branch push instead of kit pull-request
>creation.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Case (b) does not exclude main, while case (c), which creates the kit branch and pull request, is
>reached only when case (b) does not match. The review protocol and builder brief return the tree to
>main after a mission, making it the normal starting state for an apply. The protected-branch
>ruleset refuses a direct push to main, and the engine's _apply_not_landed treats the resulting
>kit not applied reply as a pipeline stop.
>
> > [src/hands/kit.py\[222-257\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/kit.py/#L222-L257) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2085-2097\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2085-L2097) > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[275-286\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L275-L286) > [src/hands/kit.py\[222-256\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/kit.py/#L222-L256) > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[461-469\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L461-L469) > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[105-125\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L105-L125) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Case (b) of `PULL_REQUEST_APPLY` matches `main` as an in-flight mission branch. An apply started on `main`, the normal state between missions, therefore attempts a direct push to protected `main` instead of creating the kit branch and pull request. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/kit.py[222-257] >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[91-128] >- DESIGN.md[3750-3790] > >## Recommended Fix >Explicitly exclude `main` from case (b), so an apply starting there proceeds through case (c). Update the matching prompt text in DESIGN.md and the handbook, update tests that pin the wording, and add a test asserting that case (b) excludes `main`. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

3. Stalled checks can exceed the tool timeout ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>ci_wait starts its nine-minute deadline only after authentication, origin, pull-request and rules
>reads, each of which can consume a subprocess timeout, and it starts a further checks read without
>bounding it by the remaining time. When those commands stall, one foreground call can run well
>beyond the stated nine minutes and exceed the role's tool-call timeout before returning a wait or
>error result.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/cli.py[R232-235]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-b53aaafe941dad7529e17dc5ad20b86fb13177f2778fbe0547c019ca0c4c8ce4R232-R235) > >```diff >+ deadline = clock() + limit_s >+ while True: >+ try: >+ reported = forge.pr_checks(gh, repo, pr) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>The deadline excludes setup and fails to bound polling by remaining time, contradicting the
>command’s nine-minute guarantee.
>
> > [PR-#8](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/8) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The deadline is set after four setup reads, while forge gives subprocesses a 120-second timeout by
>default; the polling read also uses that default after the deadline has been set. The new command
>promises a nine-minute foreground call.
>
> > [src/hands/cli.py\[187-190\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/cli.py/#L187-L190) > [src/hands/cli.py\[217-257\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/cli.py/#L217-L257) > [src/hands/forge.py\[23-24\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/forge.py/#L23-L24) > [src/hands/forge.py\[52-66\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/forge.py/#L52-L66) > [src/hands/forge.py\[90-95\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/forge.py/#L90-L95) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The nine-minute limit excludes setup subprocesses and the final checks subprocess, so a stalled call can outlast its foreground tool timeout. >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/cli.py[217-257] >- src/hands/forge.py[52-59] >- src/hands/forge.py[90-95] >## Recommended Fix >Start the deadline before setup and pass the remaining time as a timeout to every blocking subprocess, including the final poll. Return an appropriate waiting or error result when no time remains. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
4. Test subprocesses can hang indefinitely ✓ Resolved
>
>Description >
> >
>The new test fixtures invoke git and gh through subprocess.run without an explicit timeout. A
>stalled local tool can block the test suite indefinitely, including repository setup in
>tests/test_ci_wait.py and tests/test_doctor.py.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[tests/test_ci_wait.py[R47-51]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-36b7a4554465cfd4b0a4732939dec54773485e077f026a2d7d9c98ee7ed82e0dR47-R51) > >```diff >+ subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(root)], check=True) >+ subprocess.run( >+ ["git", "-C", str(root), "remote", "add", "origin", "https://github.com/o/r.git"], >+ check=True, >+ ) >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Added synchronous subprocess calls lack required explicit timeouts under the repository’s active
>compliance rule.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Compliance rule 3263087 requires synchronous process calls to have explicit timeouts. The added test
>subprocess calls shown in these files use subprocess.run without any timeout argument, while the
>production calls and wheel-build helper do provide timeouts.
>
> > Rule 3263087: [Do not start background processes; run with explicit timeouts in foreground](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3263087?state=active) > [tests/test_ci_wait.py\[47-51\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/tests/test_ci_wait.py/#L47-L51) > [tests/test_ci_wait.py\[186-188\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/tests/test_ci_wait.py/#L186-L188) > [tests/test_doctor.py\[3580-3581\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/tests/test_doctor.py/#L3580-L3581) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >Several new test subprocess calls omit explicit timeouts, so a stalled `git` or fake `gh` process can hang the quality gate indefinitely. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- tests/test_ci_wait.py[47-51] >- tests/test_ci_wait.py[186-188] >- tests/test_ci_wait.py[369-381] >- tests/test_doctor.py[3580-3581] > >## Recommended Fix >Add a bounded `timeout` argument to every new `subprocess.run` call, using a short test-appropriate limit and preserving the existing assertions and error handling. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >
5. A missing pull request hides its review 🐞 Bug ≡ Correctness
>
>Description >
> >
>The no-open-PR branch of the review protocol writes a blocker file but, under pull_request,
>explicitly commits it nowhere even if the mission branch exists. When that blocker stops the
>pipeline, the architect is instructed to read the review from the mission branch, where the file is
>absent.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[R64-65]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-1a13ad1e2168d9dd38e2e3f07712fc77e6d7bbef5b55f45f54dbd1737103bfb6R64-R65) > >```diff >+ it as below, and reply with `blockers=1 should-fix=0`. With `pull_request` >+ it is committed nowhere: `main` refuses it, and the branch may not exist. >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>The documented no-PR path leaves the blocker unavailable where the architect is instructed to read
>it.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>The new no-PR instruction says the file is committed nowhere, whereas the unreadable-rules path
>explicitly permits a commit to an existing mission branch. The handbook's blocker route directs the
>architect to read that file from origin/<branch>.
>
> > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[26-35\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L26-L35) > [templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md\[61-65\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md/#L61-L65) > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[1159-1161\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L1159-L1161) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >A no-pull-request blocker review is not committed even when its mission branch exists, leaving the architect's documented read path empty. >## Fix Focus Areas >- templates/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[61-65] >- meta/REVIEW-PROTOCOL.md[61-65] >## Recommended Fix >Check whether the named mission branch exists and commit the blocker review there when it does, as the unreadable-rules path already directs. Specify a usable handoff when no branch exists. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

6. Kits can still weaken the gate their PR merges on 🐞 Bug ⛨ Security
>
>Description >
> >
>carries_ci only treats an entry as CI when its casefolded path begins with .github/ or equals
>scripts/check. The gate that scripts/check runs (uv sync, ruff check ., pytest) is also
>configured by pyproject.toml, uv.lock and tests/conftest.py. An architect-filed kit that
>changes one of those files (for example pytest addopts, a conftest that deselects tests, or ruff
>excludes) is still approved by the engine without a human hold, and its own pull request's check
>then runs the weakened gate it merges on, which is the exact risk §45's hold is meant to close.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[src/hands/spool.py[R173-183]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-afef6fe420dcdc67164710839c508470d94b5a42c23284c4d8cbca7fe9a71221R173-R183) > >```diff >+CI_PREFIX = ".github/" >+#: …and so does the gate script every hands brief names. >+CI_GATE = "scripts/check" >+ >+ >+def carries_ci(entry: str) -> bool: >+ """§45: the one test of whether a kit entry carries the repository's CI — its >+ path, casefolded, begins `.github/` or equals `scripts/check`. The engine's hold >+ (`Spool.stored_kit_ci`) and `hands kit check`'s `WARN ci:` line ask this.""" >+ folded = entry.casefold() >+ return folded.startswith(CI_PREFIX) or folded == CI_GATE >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>Gate configuration files can alter the checks that approve their own merge, matching the stated
>security rationale.
>
> > [PR-#7](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/7) > > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>scripts/check runs uv sync --extra dev, uv run ruff check . and uv run pytest, so its
>behaviour depends on the project and test configuration in the kit's own branch.
>_carries_no_owner_entry holds a kit only when stored_kit_ci (that is, carries_ci) names an
>entry, so changes to those other files are auto-approved. The handbook text added in this PR states
>the rationale: a PR's check runs the gate script from its own branch, so a kit that rewrote it could
>weaken its own check.
>
> > [scripts/check\[1-22\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/scripts/check/#L1-L22) > [src/hands/spool.py\[171-183\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/spool.py/#L171-L183) > [src/hands/playbook.py\[2558-2597\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/src/hands/playbook.py/#L2558-L2597) > [docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md\[147-162\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md/#L147-L162) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >`carries_ci` treats only `.github/` and `scripts/check` as the repository's CI. The gate that `scripts/check` runs is also driven by `pyproject.toml` (pytest/ruff config, dependencies), `uv.lock` and `tests/conftest.py`, so a role-filed kit that touches them is engine-approved and can weaken its own PR's check. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- src/hands/spool.py[171-183] >- src/hands/kit.py[1003-1015] >- docs/ARCHITECT-HANDBOOK.md[147-162] > >## Recommended Fix >Extend `carries_ci` to also match (casefolded) `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, any `conftest.py`, and `scripts/` as a whole, or a configurable list. Update the hold reason text, the handbook and DESIGN wording, and the tests to match. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

7. Mission metadata breaks its own edit rule 📘 Rule violation § Compliance
>
>Description >
> >
>The PR modifies meta/plan.md and meta/CHECKPOINT.md while the updated checkpoint states that
>sub-agents must not edit either file. The U0 metadata changes therefore leave the mission plan and
>checkpoint outside the repository's stated authoring constraint.
>
>
>
>Code >
> >[meta/plan.md[R1-3]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/pull/9/files#diff-7b1c6ea9ab4fd6179a8304348a94fbf1fa61cfb6aafed7ec549bcd7b7f8df461R1-R3) > >```diff >+# plan — mission 29 (a `main` that takes pull requests only) > >-Source: meta/BUILDER-28-PROMPT.md, DESIGN v3.27 §44 (with §6, §10, §19, >-§31, §32, §33, §36, §38, §39, §43), meta/reviews/REVIEW-27.md, >-meta/findings/FINDINGS.md (H-077, H-078). Branch `mission-28`, created from >-`main` (b943019, `plan: mission 28 kit (DESIGN v3.27, a pause that holds >-the next step)`). Units run in order; each ends with a commit and a push to >-`mission-28`; the last unit opens the pull request, reads the hosted >-review, and returns the tree to `main`. `[x]` = done and pushed, `[b]` = >-blocked (two failures) or refused. >+Source: meta/BUILDER-29-PROMPT.md, DESIGN v3.28 §45 (with §4, §6, §8, §10, >``` >
>
>Relevance >
> > `●●● Strong` > >
>The finding identifies a direct violation of an explicit active metadata-authoring constraint.
>
> > ⓘ Recommendations generated based on similar findings in past PRs >
>
>Evidence >
> >
>Compliance rule 3263089 prohibits sub-agent changes to meta/plan.md and meta/CHECKPOINT.md. Both
>files are modified in this PR, and the checkpoint's standing constraints explicitly state that
>sub-agents do not edit them.
>
> > Rule 3263089: [Sub-agents must not modify plan/checkpoint metadata files](https://app.qodo.ai/rules/3263089?state=active) > [meta/plan.md\[1-10\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/meta/plan.md/#L1-L10) > [meta/CHECKPOINT.md\[65-70\]](https://github.com/SigorMatt/hands/blob/e3756303fbb6dc0a7d21ddd365f7c81357b7fd14/meta/CHECKPOINT.md/#L65-L70) >
>
>Agent prompt >
> >``` >The issue below was found during a code review. Follow the provided context and guidance below and implement a solution > >## Issue description >The PR changes `meta/plan.md` and `meta/CHECKPOINT.md` even though the mission's standing constraints prohibit sub-agents from editing those metadata files. > >## Fix Focus Areas >- meta/plan.md[1-10] >- meta/CHECKPOINT.md[3-12] > >## Recommended Fix >Have the coordinating process own plan and checkpoint updates, and prevent sub-agent commits from including `meta/plan.md` or `meta/CHECKPOINT.md`; if these changes are required, record them as coordinator-authored changes rather than sub-agent edits. >``` > ⓘ Copy this prompt and use it to remediate the issue with your preferred AI generation tools >

### The AI Code Review Platform

## Get Started
Simply sign into Github and click the "Configure" button. Check out our documentation for more info: https://docs.qodo.ai/get-started.

## Overview
Qodo automatically reviews every GitHub pull request, identifies logic bugs, edge cases, security issues, and code quality problems, and provides actionable suggestions your team can apply immediately.

Install in minutes. Integrates seamlessly into your existing workflows.

## Qodo is designed for developers who:
- Handle frequent pull requests and need reliable review coverage
- Balance code quality with fast delivery
- Work in complex, multi-repo systems
- Use AI-generated code and need stronger guardrails
- Build production software where reliability matters

## Qodo Capabilities
- ## Automated PR Analysis
  - Reviews every pull request automatically
  - No manual trigger required

- ## Context-Aware Code Review
  - Understands cross-file changes
  - Detects architectural inconsistencies
